operational-example.copy: Use List to scan comparable records when each row leads to detail, action, or review.

scenario.title: Movement review queue
rationale: List keeps repeated operational items scannable before a table is needed.
Rows keep icon, label, metadata, and value aligned without inventing a card per item.
Use Table when comparison needs columns, sorting, or bulk action.

items.rule: Owns grouping, width, border, and row rhythm.
Carries one navigable or readable record.
Supports record type without replacing the label.
Use concise name and secondary context.
Optional aligned amount or status value.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, loading, error, selected, hover, default
items: Use list semantics for non-tabular records.
Use buttons or links when rows navigate or act.
Keep visible labels; icons are never the only row name.
Expose selected state when row selection changes behavior.
Do not rely on color alone for error or selected state.

variants.copy: List variants describe row density and job: standard records, compact logs, action rows, status rows, and media rows.

states.copy: List states communicate availability, selection, loading, error, hover, and default readability.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines the row job; state defines interaction and feedback without changing the list structure.

full-width.copy: List can fill its parent when used in sheets, cards, and detail panes.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use one column across viewports; density changes row rhythm, not the information order.

viewport-organization.copy: List works best where records need vertical scanning before comparison.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use one comfortable column with strong labels.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use in panels or sheets with visible metadata.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact lists for logs; switch to Table for comparison.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify variant, state, interactivity, visible value, and row icon behavior.

api-foundations.copy: List API exposes item data, variant, state, selection, and action model while Design System owns row rhythm and semantics.

props.name: state
props.type: default | hover | selected | loading | error | disabled
props.notes: List-wide fallback state for demos or controlled examples.

props.name: interactive
props.notes: Renders rows as buttons when a row acts or navigates.

props.name: density
props.notes: Row density from Flow density context.

props.name: onSelect
props.notes: Called when an interactive row is selected.

groups.title: Use
items: Escalate to Table when comparison needs columns.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not fake tables with lists.
Do not hide row names behind icons.
Do not nest cards inside rows.

rejectIf: List is used for tabular comparison.

miel.copy: MIEL treats List as repeated record structure: agents may place it for scan-first records, but humans confirm navigation, selection, and when Table is required.
canDecide: Use List for movements, notifications, audit snippets, and support queues.
Use compact density for logs with short metadata.
Use status rows when risk or availability changes the row meaning.
mustAsk: Rows need bulk actions or column comparison.
A row action changes money, permissions, or status.
Selection changes downstream filters or process.
rejectIf: The list hides required row labels.
The agent uses List where Table is needed.
miel.handoff: I am using List for repeated records. Please confirm row action, selection behavior, metadata priority, and whether this should become Table.
